utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And did Zigic work as a guard at first, or you don't know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I don't know exactly whether he worked as a guard but he did -- he was coming there, but I don't think that he worked there as a guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And these shifts at first were 24-hour shifts, a full day, these guards, one group, let's say Crni's group, and then another group would come and stay for 24 hours? Was that so in these first days, as you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I don't understand that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Let me put it this way: At first when you said that there were only two groups of guards, these guards worked in 24-hour intervals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: No? How long did they work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Approximately 20 -- no, 12. Then some -- then they would go home to get some rest, and the other group would come. The group that gave -- that provided assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: A group for providing assistance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes. Remember we talked about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Oh, I remember. So they were not regular guards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: That is correct. They came at night.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So in those first days, they provided security?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: They provided assistance. For instance, like that friend of mine Sava, and when he saw us there in the camp he started crying, threw away the weapon, and went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You said that later on, there were three shifts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When, approximately, these three shifts became established?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: They were also going 12 hours apiece, and then they would go home, rest, and the next day they were the first shift, and then the second shift, and those who had -- who were on the night shift would go and have 24 hours off to rest off. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When were these three shifts established, approximately, in relation to your date of arrival at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: That's an awkward question, and a lot of questions have been asked of me and I don't know if I can say 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Of course I'm not asking you about the exact date, especially in the light of what you have gone through there, and following nine years, I understand fully that you cannot remember everything. I'm asking you for an approximation. We know that everything you are saying is an approximation given the amount of time that has passed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes. Nine years have passed by, it's a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Of course. So please, if you can do your best to put it in time for me.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can we say two -- after about two weeks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes. Two, three weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to another issue. When you arrived, you were in Room 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes. This is what we started calling it later. It wasn't called that at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So it was an internal designation that you introduced?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: No, it wasn't really us. It was them. They designated it as 1, 2, 3, 4. As more and more prisoners, inmates arrived, they expanded. For instance, when they were gathering people from Kozarac, then a large group came and --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Very well, we'll come to that later.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: But for two days we were in Room 2 --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And then you were moved to Room 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: After interrogation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And after having stayed in Room 1 for a few days, you moved to Room 4 and this is where you stayed until the end?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, with the cooperation of the interpreters, we are going to be working until 5.00, so we are going to take a break until -- a break at a quarter to 4.00 for 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So along with -- you spent all that time with Witness B there, in other words, you together came to Room 2, then to Room 1, and then transferred to Room 4?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I assume that you were with Witness B throughout the day every day? It would make sense.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Well, we did not hold hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Of course. But you were there. Nobody was going there, he wasn't going anywhere, you weren't going there, excluding interrogation of course?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Occasionally one could go from one room to another room.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How did you two move to Room 4?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I think he came to me and he said: "Do you want to come to Room 4?" I said "Why?" He said, "We're all going so why don't you come along too."

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether somebody had told him to go there, suggested to go, or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: They probably did, but I don't know. I didn't even know about it until he mentioned it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did three shifts start operating at the time when you moved to Room 4 or perhaps a little bit before that time or a little bit after that time? And as we are not saying things in -- putting things in an accurate way --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: You are saying that it's inaccurate. I cannot say that it's inaccurate. I cannot know the exact time, the exact hour. We didn't have a calendar or a watch.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, this is why I'm trying to relate it to a certain event like your move to Room 4. So was it around that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: What event now?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I think that we had a misunderstanding. I'm going to try to explain it to you again. My question to you is: Because you cannot recall a date, which I understand and fully respect given the amount of time that has passed, can we say that you moved to Room 4 approximately a day plus/minus, but around the time when three shifts started operating?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: When the people from Kozarac were gathered, this is when the third room was established. There were too many of us in the first and second. We couldn't breathe anymore. The air was too stuffy.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Let's try it this way. Kozarac took -- happened in late May; is that correct? They gathered these people around in late May, and in the very first days of June, they were already there. They were already detained.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I could not tell you exactly. These -- at that time, we were in -- also in fear. We were a bit lost. Too lost to be able to say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this might be the right moment for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it is. We'll take a break until 4.00. Witness E, you are reminded not to discuss your evidence with anybody during the break including members of the Prosecution team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness E, you repeatedly said today that brothers Banovic were on Crni's shift, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Will you tell me, please, will you please try to describe Crni once again? What did he look like, how did he dress?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I think he was about 170 tall. I never measured him, so I can't really know. And he was always in a black T-shirt, short sleeves, short hair, dark, well-built.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you used to see that man around the town before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Once or twice perhaps, on a motorbike or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What kind of a motorbike?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: He rode a Kawasaki.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you frequent Zvejzdas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And where did you see him around the town, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Somewhere near the fly-over.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tomo Prodan, does that ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You don't know a man called Tomo Prodan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I didn't really know people's names.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever discuss a person called Tomo Prodan with your brother? Perhaps he knew him.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And what does this Banovic who used this baseball bat look like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Well, he was on the short side with long hair.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Was there anything characteristic about him, something else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I couldn't really say now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned today you -- on several occasions you mentioned an event or rather the incident with Jovo Radocaj, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I know that his first name was Jovo. What was his last name, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: At the time when he was beaten, you stood in the doorway of your dormitory and watched it, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: What do you mean? What does "doorway" mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You were in the door, I mean the door frame?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Well, I was slightly over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: On the inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So you -- as you testified today, you saw that Banovic hit -- Banovic hit Jovo with his bat 10 or perhaps 12 times?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Well, I didn't stand there all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But you saw him beat him, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And before that, if I remember well, you said today how he called him out?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We could not hear the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness E, your answers are not being picked up by the interpreter. Would you please move forward closer to the microphone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Will that be all right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: A while ago you described how he was taken from Room 1 towards your room, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: There in front of your room is where the incident that we are talking about happened. Will you please give us an answer? Will you please say yes or no? Don't just nod your head because the interpreters cannot interpret that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I saw Banovic beat him when he brought him into that passage or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What passage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Well, that passage of Room 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: He brought him from some other place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes. He brought him there. He took him over to the weigh bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So they took him towards the weigh bridge from the direction of Room 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: From number 1 or from 2. No, from number 4 towards the weigh bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Now, let us try to figure this out. This morning you said they took him from the direction of Rooms 1 and 2 towards Room 4.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: This morning I said they called him out from Room 4. He wasn't in Room 1. He was in Room 4. And they took him up there, and then they beat him on the way from there to here, from 1 to 4. I think that is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Right. And you said it was during Crni's shift?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And who carried Jovo into that room where you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: They brought him into that passage there, and then they told three or four of our inmates to carry him away.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember one of those detainees who carried him in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Then when you testified about Drago Tokmadzic's death, you said how you saw a hearse take him away in the morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Well, not really in the morning. He first lay there for sometime until they arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you see, perhaps, a woman, a physician come in the morning to establish his death? Did you see any of the policemen who were not any of the regular guards in the Keraterm there that morning? Will you please say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: No, I did not see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: This morning you spoke about the incident involving Car. In the beginning of your examination, you described in detail who beat him and you said it was Ziga and Duca. Was Crni there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes, Crni was there and Keli too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Today you told us about this event in detail, but later on, when my learned friend from the Prosecution asked you about Kajin, you then said, "Maybe," "Perhaps," "I think so," something to that effect, that you also saw Kajin there. You made several statements as it has already been established about that, and today during your direct examination, until the Prosecutor asked you about Kajin, you also told us about that without ever mentioning this detail, and I'll read you some of that. This is a statement of the 20th -- no, let's start from the statement that you made in February 1995 which is three years after you left Keraterm. You said as follows: "I saw Zigic and Duca beat Car. There were present other guards, but I cannot remember the names and I cannot describe others who were there. I was in Room 2. The beating took place and I watched it with others from a distance of 16 metres." That is what you said in February 1995. Then in August this year, and at this interview the -- my learned friend from the Prosecution who examined you today was present also, and you describe in detail the beating of Car. "Crni, Zigic, Duca also took part in this." That is identical as you told us today. You said, "There were also others who beat Car, but I cannot remember who they were." So in none of your statements, three years after that or the statement that you made a few months ago, August last year, you never mentioned Kajin.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: No, I don't, because he was the commander there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So you -- the first time you mentioned that Kajin was present was in the conversation with the Prosecutor a few days ago. How is it that you suddenly remembered it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Well, one can always remember something.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But how did you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I don't know, but I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Wouldn't it be true that you are not sure whether he was there or wasn't; would you allow such a possibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Kajin was there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me then where did Kajin stand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I think as there was a bunker -- there was a bunker there and they were beating him there, and he was behind them. From my angle I think he was behind them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Will you take it slowly and tell us where did you stand? Where was Car beaten? Where did you stand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I was in dormitory 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And who was there with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: All the detainees.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Was your brother there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: He was there too, but he wasn't with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Was there somebody else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Well, I'm telling you all the detainees were there, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Right. Do you want me to give you names?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: No, there is no need to. So everybody watched it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And they all saw what you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Well, they should have, unless they had their heads down or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So where did this thing happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Right next to the bunker, next to the weigh bridge, the weigh bridge is slightly in front of it. I'm talking about Keraterm. The weigh bridge is in front of -- they were next to the bunker, whether they called it the bunker or something, but it is -- that is where it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown Prosecutor's Exhibit 2B, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Will you please -- will you show us on this photograph where did you stand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: This is dormitory 2, and I was inside, perhaps two or three metres Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. away, to the right if you now face the building, right here where I'm pointing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So two or three metres behind the door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: No, not behind the door because the door was open.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But inside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes, inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And where were others? Behind you, next to you, in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Well, they were all there next to me, behind me. There was perhaps one in front of me, only one, maybe one, perhaps just one. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And where were Ziga, Duca, and Crni? Where were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: You can't see it on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Let us then try with Exhibit 2G. Would that be more or less the view from dormitory 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Will you have 2B again, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave may we just look for the right photograph? Could you please put this photograph -- show this photograph to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: This is a photograph of a model. Can you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Right. Now, will you show on this photograph where was Ziga, Crni?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Here, at this corner here. Can you see it, this door here? That is Room 2. This is number 2, the door right next to this larger room, and they were here, directly at the bunker, and as you look from the dormitory, the bunker is to the left, and they were to the left of the bunker. And that is in front of the bunker that he ran in circles and carried this machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And now just tell me when is it that you saw Kajin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Well, Kajin was there all the time. He was there all day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But you just -- you say all day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So perhaps you saw him before that and perhaps you saw him after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: He was there all the time, next to that bunker. They were all there by the bunker watching Car circling.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about all of them. I'm asking about Kajin.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: And I'm telling you that Kajin was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Will you please show us exactly where is it that he stood when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Well, I do not know the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'm not saying the time. I'm asking about the place. That is where he was all the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes, all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And how long did it all take?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, did it take a couple of minutes or --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Can't say. It could be couple of minutes and it could have been a couple of hours. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. In August were you interviewed in detail about Kajin's role in that -- in Keraterm by the investigators, that is my learned friend from the Prosecution? Did he ask you in detail about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Well, he was the shift commander at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: That is not what I'm asking you. I'm asking you whether you spoke in detail about Kajin's role in Keraterm in August when the investigators interviewed you, visited you, headed by my learned friend?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Well, we discussed it. Whether it was in great detail or not, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But you answered all the questions about Kajin that the Prosecutor asked you?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness says yes, the interpreters believe, because he's away from the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But you answered to the best of your recollection at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters believe the witness said yes because he is away from the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And on that occasion, you were also asked details about Car?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Again, I ask -- the interpreters are having difficulty hearing your answers, so please stay closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion you were asked in detail also about the incident concerning Car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And on that occasion you said who took part in that and who was present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Well, yes, but I couldn't remember all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: For the last time, I'm asking you to explain it to us. How is it that you remembered it on the 23rd of March, 2001, nine years later, and after so many previous questions about Car and Kajin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: How? Well, I wouldn't know myself, but whatever, I just remembered.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I put it to you that you are not sure that you saw Kajin there and that you are now affirming something that you did not see or, at best, what you are not sure about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I do affirm that Kajin was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Right. Let us move on to some other topics. You mentioned that in Keraterm, Faca killed a man. What was that man's name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I didn't mention that he killed a man. A man, relative of the killed person came to me. He lived in Brezicani, and he said that Faca had killed his relative in the WC.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When I say "mentioned," I mean you mentioned it today during the examination. I don't mean anything else. What was that man's name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I will refresh your memory if I tell you that his name is Muharem Nadarevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Oh, perhaps I didn't understand what you said who it was who told me that. Did you ask me who was killed or who told me that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Who was killed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: But Muharem Nadarevic wasn't killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What was the name of the man who was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, after the incident that you described, that is, after the murder or the massacre, whatever you care to call it in Room 3, in the morning Cupo came to your room and asked, "Are there any wounded?"

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: He did not enter the room. He was next to the edge of the building, and he said then, "Are there any wounded?" And one guy who was wounded by the ricocheted bullet casing said that he'd been wounded and so he said that he was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And at that point, Cupo's shift wasn't on duty, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I remembered it later. I remember it later that they had taken over the duty. I did not remember it at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But in your statement of 15th August, you said the following, "I remember that in the morning after the massacre, Cupo Banovic turned up at the doorway to my room and asked if there were any wounded."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Next sentence, "I don't know why he was in the camp because his shift was not on duty that morning." So when is it that you remembered? Is it that you again remembered it a few days ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Not a few days ago, today.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But this is the statement that you made in August last year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: There appears to be no French interpretation. Do we have French interpretation? Yes. Yes, we now have French interpretation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You and your brother told that man not to come out, but he wanted to come out, I mean the wounded man.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And that same evening, a new massacre took place, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And that night, Crni was on duty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Well, that was the shift. That's the shift, the one that stayed on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So now let's try it this way. The second massacre took place the next night; am I right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: At what time of the night approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Around 3.00 or thereabouts. That was it. I don't know exactly, because I had no way of determining that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But -- and Crni's shift was on at that time. That is what you said.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly what shift. Perhaps it was another shift that day and they came back nevertheless.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned this incident that happened, and I am going back to the pre-war situation. The incident that you had with Kajin in a restaurant at the railway station, or what is it, a coffee shop or something. There was a clash between the two of you, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And there was another guy with him. And who paid the piper to put it that way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: They won.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you exchange some blows, were there any fisticuffs or something?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I read you two statements, and I conclude from them that Kajin was the ones who fared worse.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Well, if you say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In your first statement you said that you had an argument with him. In the second one you said you had a fight, which one is right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: The second, we got into a fight.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Your statement -- your August statement says, "Before the war I knew him superficially, but once I gave him a beating. Once I beat him." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Well, we got into a fight. Now who got the beating, really I cannot say. But be that as it may, the two of them fled.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if you hit him once, more?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Well, I guess so. I can't really remember because it could have been, I don't know, 12, 13 years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you remember where did you hit him? Do you -- can you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, can I then conclude that you held a grudge against one another?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: No, never. Nothing, nothing before that or after that. Except that he refused to pay that woman for the use of lavatory. I told him, "Why don't you pay that?" And then they jumped, "Why are you meddling? Stop it." And that is how we came to fists.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But on the first -- initially when you arrived at Keraterm, you were afraid to meet face to face with Kajin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Because earlier some men had come and, for instance, he slapped him and others brought him out and beat him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So they were taking out revenge on people for what he had done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes, I said for a slap.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that Kajin did nothing to avenge himself on you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did he say that no one was to touch you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: He said as follows: "I am not one of those who will bear a grudge." I don't know how to explain it. "So I'm not one of those who will seek revenge."

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: So this happened between men. And he said, "Had you had weapons on, I would have killed you, but while I was -- while I'm here, nobody can touch you."

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to the weapons used during the attack on Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Carrying our arms in general. I didn't even know about the attack on Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: After that, did you have some courage to get out after you talked to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes. After that I had no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Until then you did not come out at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: That was at the very beginning for the first two or three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did Kajin treat anyone else in this way, this fair and protective way, if I can put it that way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Well, he did not allow just anyone to be bothered.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You mean was it only the people whom he knew, or he did not pay attention, he did not discriminate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: He said those who were innocent, he said that those who were innocent would not be bothered.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In one of your statements of 1995, you said that Kajin was too soft with the prisoners. What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Let me read it to you. The statement is from 1995, that is the one from February. "I think that they believed that Kajin was too soft on detainees, and he was relieved after I don't know how many days."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Most probably he was on the side of the people who had not done anything. He was protecting them. He probably knew that some of these people did not do anything or had nothing to do with some things. For instance, that attack on Prijedor, on whatever these people called it, I don't know what people did and who was involved in what. First of all, we Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. didn't even know why we were being taken to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: At that time you said Kajin allowed doctors to treat you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. And we asked for pills, and in fact a man who was missing an arm would come with medicines and other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did Kajin call him to come?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes. We told Kajin what we needed and then he did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When Kajin was on duty, were there any problems -- and when he was present, were there any problems about going to the toilet? Did you have any problems in that regard? If you don't know, I'll just withdraw the question. You mentioned a moment ago that Kajin was present during another incident when someone called Sistek -- was that Samir Sistek?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes. He was from Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When he was taken out. And Kajin was not present when he was taken out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: He was there, to the side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. I'm referring to the moment when he was called out from the room, when he was taken out of the room, when Sistek and another man were taken out, Kajin was not present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: He was present, off to the side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean to the side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: He was to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you please describe this to the left? To the left of what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: When I looked out the room, Room number 2, straight to the right were Duca and Zigic, and I don't know how many were there. There was one with a red beret, I didn't know how many men were there. We couldn't even see all of them. And I saw first they made this Kocijas to sing some songs and he did. And then it was, "Let's see, guys, how brave you are, how you can fight." So they asked they fight each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But who was it who was calling them out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: It was Zigic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And who was telling them, "Come on guys, let's see"? Who was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Zigic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And who demanded that they fight each other?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Zigic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And what time of the day was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: It was around the nightfall. I cannot say exactly whether it was 8.00, 9.00 or 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Was that the time around the point when the shifts were changing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How long did this last?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Approximately half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you just tell me when did you recall that incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: It sort of came to me, I don't know exactly, but I remembered it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When did it happen, on the 23rd of May? What incident -- I apologise. Now, the incident I'm referring to now --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Oh, I've known that from the beginning when I first arrived, since I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: My question to you is --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Oh, you mean when I remembered?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Perhaps last year.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you know about that incident in August last year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When the Prosecutor asked you about Kajin in great detail and comprehensively, why didn't you tell him that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I didn't think of it. There are many things that I still haven't said.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did he ask you in detail about Kajin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: He asked me approximately what shifts there were, who was shift commander, whether Kajin was shift commander, whether he was shift commander, camp commander, things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did he ask you whether Kajin took part in any of the incidents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Why didn't you say it then, that -- what you said now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Well, he didn't take part. He just observed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But did he, my friend, ask you whether he was present? And knowing that he is professional, I'm sure that he would have asked you whether he was present at the incident.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I don't know. Maybe I made some kind of mistake, perhaps. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You said a mistake. What does it mean? You did not remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I guess I did not remember at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How long did this interview last?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did this interview last half an hour, 15 minutes? Your interview with the -- my learned colleague who examined you today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: You mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: No, no. I'm not referring to the examination today. The interview with the Prosecutor in August last year.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I don't know, five or six hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And in these five or six hours of conversation and recollection, you could not remember what you just told us today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Questions are one thing and answers are another thing. A person forgets things.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Let me sum up. The same person asked you the same question and you gave different answers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I recalled what I had seen. I did not lie about anything. And I did not say anything that was untrue but only things that I remembered and that I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Today you said this: During the first days, at first, Kajin was the camp commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Then when I asked you, when I asked you to explain to me what the first days or the beginning meant to you, you said that it could have been a couple of days or five or six days, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes. It was couple of days or approximately five to six days.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When you said the first days you meant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: When we first came to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So the first couple of days are the first five or six days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: To my learned friend, Mr. Greaves, you said that this was 25 days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: From where?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: That Kajin was the camp commander for 25 days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I said that in the first days there were no problems, that we were --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I wasn't asking you about problems. I was asking you about who the camp commander was. You said five or six days, then about an hour ago you said 25 days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I said that he was relieved of duty 20 -- I'm saying 25 days before he was relieved of duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Let me try -- perhaps we don't understand each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the indulgence of the Trial Chamber, I think this is an important point. I would like to take it from the top.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Continue, if you can do it quickly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: This morning you said that Kajin was the commander at Keraterm in the first days, in the beginning. Then when I asked you -- when I asked you to explain what the first days -- what the beginning was, you said five to six days; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: You asked me what it means a couple of days. That's all you asked me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I had asked you and we discussed it at some length, what it meant to you the couple of days and the first days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes, and I explained it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When we bring these two together, the first days, and what it means to you, the first days or the first couple of days, we come to Kajin being the commander for five or six days or I don't understand you at all.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Kajin was the commander until Sikirica arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: That is not in dispute, we agree on that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I think it went on longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What I'm interested in knowing is exactly how much time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: We did not have the calendar or a watch. I can say one, two, five, 15, 50 days. To me it was all the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You said in the beginning in the first days --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, I think we -- I think you've covered that sufficiently. You have been on this point for quite some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your indulgence and with my utmost respect, if you can indulge me for a couple more questions only. Just to try to clarify it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You said that in the first days at the beginning, the command -- he was the commander, and then you said that it was 25 days. You spent a total of two months in Keraterm. For you, the beginning is the first half of your stay in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: He was there from the first day when we entered and the next day until the evening, and then in the evening he was relieved by Sikirica. I don't know how many days it was. I don't know. We can say -- it's very thought-involving this whole thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on. At first who were the shift commanders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Kajin was, in this one shift, and I don't know about the others. I don't know about the other two shifts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: At first were you locked up by Kajin and then the next night by Crni?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I cannot recall now, but the door was closed. I don't know whether the door was locked.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In these first days, did you see Kajin at night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Perhaps at first until they got organised. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one moment, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When Sikirica arrived, how many times did you see Kajin after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, once, twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In your statement from August last year, you said this: "After that, I saw Kajin in the camp on only one more occasion. Perhaps he came more often."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: After?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking after Sikirica.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Perhaps once. He may have come more often.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Just three quick questions. In the beginning, if you can tell me, you who were detained there, did you receive food from your homes? Did somebody come to the gate to deliver something?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps remember one occasion when a soldier drove up to the camp and pulled out a zolja and tried to fire it at you inside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And can you tell me one more thing: Do you remember whether there was some special lighting in Keraterm? Were there any floodlights?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: After that massacre, yes, there were some floodlights.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall whether Zigic was also detained, locked up in one of these rooms at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember a person named Maroslic whom Zigic released from prison in exchange for money?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I don't know who that person is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ryneveld.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Your Honours, before Mr. Vucicevic starts, I just wondered, in light of the extensive cross-examination on statements which the witness didn't have an opportunity to see, and because there may be some issues of credibility that the Court may want to take into account as a result of cross-examination, whether the statements to which the witness was cross-examined on ought not now be marked as exhibits in these proceedings, especially in relation to allegations of recent recollection of events and as you know from the proofing the document that we have provided, the sources have been provided in terms of where that was provided. I think it's important for the Court that these statements to which reference has been made ought be marked as exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. We agree. Certainly. I'd like to see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I don't know -- I think we have copies now, but otherwise we can certainly provide them by tomorrow morning, but we may have enough copies now to have them marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You can do that later. Mr. Vucicevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: I will try to finish in five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think tomorrow morning. Have the night to reflect and come back refreshed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. It will be good for both the witness and myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, certain. We are going to take the adjournment now. Witness E, you are reminded not to discuss your evidence with anybody including the members of the Prosecution team. We adjourn until 9.30 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: at 4.57 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday the 29th day of March, 2001, at 9.30 a.m.
